item.title: Privacy Policy
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: http://localhost:8884.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

item.title: 'Seven men with knives': Police swarm Melbourne CBD after New Year brawl
item.dc:creator: jack.hennessy
item.content:encoded:
Police have set up a crime scene in a Melbourne CBD laneway after police said a violent brawl involving up to seven men armed with knives and machetes broke out among New Year crowds just after midnight.

Two men, aged 19 and 23, were taken to the Royal Melbourne Hospital with stab wounds. Their injuries are serious but not life-threatening, police said.

Witnesses told news.com.au the fight started near a convenience store and spilled into the laneway within seconds. One woman said she grabbed her younger sister and ran into a pub kitchen to hide.

Witness [full name] said, “People were screaming and running in every direction.”

Witness, Swanston St

Arrests made

Victoria Police arrested four men at the scene and are searching for at least three more. Detectives from the Melbourne Crime Investigation Unit have taken over the investigation.

Acting Superintendent Karen Doyle said the attack was "brazen" and urged anyone with phone footage to come forward. "There were thousands of people in the city. Someone filmed this," she said.

Police urged anyone with information or phone footage to contact Crime Stoppers at 1800 333 000.
item.excerpt:encoded: Two men are in hospital and a laneway off Swanston St remains a crime scene after a brawl involving machetes broke out just after midnight.

item.title: Hero off-duty cop dives into surf to try to save swimmer
item.dc:creator: emma.kirkwood
item.content:encoded:
An off-duty police officer has been praised for running fully clothed into heavy surf at Maroubra to reach a swimmer caught in a rip on Tuesday evening.

Senior Constable Luke Barrett, 34, was walking his dog on the sand at about 7.15pm when he saw a man waving his arms beyond the break.

He handed his dog to a stranger, grabbed a rescue board from a nearby surf club rack and paddled out. Lifeguards arrived on a jet ski minutes later and helped bring the man to shore.

I didn't think about it. You see someone going under, you go.

Senior Constable Luke Barrett

The 52-year-old swimmer was treated by paramedics and taken to Prince of Wales Hospital in a stable condition.

Beaches unpatrolled after 6pm

Surf Life Saving NSW said the beach was unpatrolled at the time and reminded swimmers that most drownings happen outside the flags and outside patrol hours.

The state recorded 47 coastal drownings last financial year, the highest number in a decade.
item.excerpt:encoded: Senior Constable Luke Barrett was walking his dog at Maroubra when he spotted a man struggling in a rip 60m offshore.

item.title: 'Threat to lives': Emergency bushfire warning for Blue Mountains towns
item.dc:creator: emma.kirkwood
item.content:encoded:
An emergency warning has been issued for parts of the Upper Blue Mountains as a bushfire burning near Mount Victoria jumped containment lines on Wednesday afternoon.

The NSW Rural Fire Service said the fire was moving northeast toward Blackheath, driven by gusty westerly winds of up to 70km/h.

If you are in the area and have not left, it is now too late. Seek shelter in a solid building as the fire arrives.

NSW RFS

What you need to know

  • The Great Western Highway is closed between Katoomba and Lithgow.
  • Blue Mountains trains are replaced by buses until further notice.
  • An evacuation centre is open at Katoomba Sports Club.
  • Total fire bans are in place for the Greater Sydney region.

More than 200 firefighters and 12 aircraft are working on the blaze, which has burnt through 3400 hectares.

The Bureau of Meteorology expects a southerly change to reach the mountains around 9pm, which may push the fire in a new direction.
item.excerpt:encoded: Residents of Mount Victoria and Blackheath have been told it is too late to leave as a fast-moving fire jumps containment lines.

item.title: Treasurer's surprise $4bn cost-of-living pitch splits Canberra
item.dc:creator: emma.kirkwood
item.content:encoded:
The federal Treasurer has floated a $4 billion cost-of-living package ahead of next month's mid-year budget update, putting pressure on the Opposition to say whether it would match it.

The package includes a second round of $300 energy bill rebates for every household and a cut to the lowest income tax rate from 16 to 15 per cent.

Speaking in Brisbane on Wednesday, the Treasurer said the measures were "targeted and responsible" and would not add to inflation.

Families are still doing it tough at the checkout and at the bowser. This is help that lands in their pocket this financial year.

The Treasurer

Crossbench wants rent relief

Independent MPs said the plan did nothing for the 2.6 million households who rent. Several are pushing for a 15 per cent lift in Commonwealth Rent Assistance.

Economists were divided. One senior bank economist said the rebates would shave 0.5 percentage points off headline inflation, as the last round did, but warned the effect would be temporary.
item.excerpt:encoded: A one-off energy rebate and a cut to the lowest tax rate are on the table, but the crossbench wants more for renters.

item.title: Daycare operator in court over alleged $2m subsidy scheme
item.dc:creator: jack.hennessy
item.content:encoded:
A Sydney childcare operator has appeared in court accused of claiming more than $2 million in federal subsidies for children who never attended her centres.

The 46-year-old woman faced Downing Centre Local Court on Thursday charged with 38 counts of obtaining a financial advantage by deception. She did not enter a plea.

Court documents allege she ran three centres in western Sydney between 2022 and 2024 and lodged attendance records for 180 children who were not enrolled.

Parents shocked

One mother whose son attended one of the centres said families had no idea. "The staff were lovely. We had no reason to think anything was wrong," she said.

Her lawyer told the court his client would "vigorously defend" the charges. She was granted bail on strict conditions and will return to court in March.
item.excerpt:encoded: Prosecutors allege the operator claimed childcare subsidies for 180 children who never attended her centres.

item.title: Streets erupt as nation's currency crashes overnight
item.dc:creator: priya.nair
item.content:encoded:
Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets of the capital after the national currency lost a third of its value against the US dollar overnight.

Banks limited withdrawals to the equivalent of $50 a day and several supermarket chains stopped trading while they repriced stock.

The central bank said it had raised its key interest rate to 60 per cent in an emergency meeting before dawn.

Advice for Australians

DFAT updated its travel advice on Thursday morning, urging Australians in the country to avoid protest areas and carry enough cash for several days.

Card payments may not work. ATMs may run out of cash. Monitor local media.

Smartraveller

Around 4000 Australians are thought to be in the country, many on working holidays.
item.excerpt:encoded: The peso lost a third of its value in 12 hours. Australian travellers in the region have been told to carry cash.

item.title: Europe's tourist hotspots cap visitor numbers ahead of summer
item.dc:creator: priya.nair
item.content:encoded:
Some of Europe's busiest destinations will cap daily visitor numbers this northern summer, with fines for tourists who turn up without a booking.

Venice will extend its day-tripper fee to 90 days and limit tour groups to 25 people. Santorini will cap cruise passengers at 8000 a day, down from 17,000 at peak.

  • Venice: €10 day-tripper fee on peak days, booked online.
  • Santorini: cruise arrivals capped at 8000 per day.
  • Barcelona: tourist tax doubled for cruise passengers staying under 12 hours.
  • Amsterdam: no new hotels approved in the city centre.

Travel agents say Australians should book key sights before they fly. "The days of wandering in are over for the big names," one Sydney agent said.
item.excerpt:encoded: Venice, Santorini and Barcelona's old town are introducing daily limits. Here's what it means for your trip.

item.title: US Senate showdown: what it means for Australia
item.dc:creator: priya.nair
item.content:encoded:
A tight vote in the US Senate this week could decide the future of billions of dollars in Pacific defence funding, including money tied to the AUKUS submarine program.

The bill needs 60 votes to pass. Party leaders say they are two votes short.

Australian officials in Washington have spent the week meeting senators from both parties.

This is about the shipyards that build the boats. If the money stalls, the timeline stalls.

Former Australian ambassador

The vote is expected on Thursday, Washington time, which is Friday morning in Australia.
item.excerpt:encoded: A vote on Pacific defence spending is down to two senators. Canberra is watching closely.

item.title: Fiji clean-up begins after cyclone tears through northern islands
item.dc:creator: priya.nair
item.content:encoded:
The clean-up has begun across northern Fiji after a category four cyclone destroyed hundreds of homes on Vanua Levu and Taveuni.

Fiji's disaster management office confirmed three deaths and said around 6000 people were in evacuation centres.

An RAAF C-130 Hercules landed in Labasa on Monday carrying water purification units, tarpaulins and medical supplies.

How to help

Australian Red Cross and Caritas have opened appeals. Aid groups say cash donations are more useful than goods.
item.excerpt:encoded: Australia has sent an RAAF C-130 with water purification kits and emergency shelter.

item.title: Aussie star's surprise Marvel return sends fans into meltdown
item.dc:creator: mia.fortescue
item.content:encoded:
Perth-born actor Lachlan Reid has sent fans into a frenzy after appearing for three seconds at the end of the new Marvel trailer.

The trailer passed 90 million views in its first 24 hours. Reid, 38, played the villain in two earlier films but was thought to have left the franchise.

I have been sworn to secrecy. My mum found out from the trailer like everyone else.

Lachlan Reid on Instagram

The film was shot partly at Disney Studios Australia in Sydney last year and opens in cinemas in May.
item.excerpt:encoded: Lachlan Reid appears for three seconds in the new trailer. That was enough to break the internet.

item.title: Surprise star spotted on superyacht on Sydney Harbour
item.dc:creator: mia.fortescue
item.content:encoded:
Ferry passengers got an unexpected show on Wednesday when US pop star Delaney Brooks was spotted swimming off a superyacht anchored near Watsons Bay.

The 92m vessel arrived in Sydney on Monday and is reportedly chartered for $1.5m a week.

Brooks, who plays three sold-out shows at Accor Stadium next week, waved to a passing Manly ferry before diving back in.

Her team declined to comment on the singer's plans.
item.excerpt:encoded: A Grammy winner was seen swimming off a $200m yacht in Watsons Bay. Ferry passengers had front-row seats.

item.title: Train delays on T1 line after signal fault at Strathfield
item.dc:creator: daniel.rossi
item.content:encoded:
commuters on the t1 north shore and western line are facing delays of up to 40 mins this morning after a signal failure near strathfield station around 6.50am

sydney trains said technicians were on site. extra buses have been arranged between strathfield and parramatta. passengers told to allow extra travel time

TK: quote from sydney trains spokesperson. TK: confirm number of services cancelled

item.title: reality star reveals
item.dc:creator: hannah.walsh
item.content:encoded:
Former reality TV contestant Brooke Saunders has revealed she was paid less than $100 a day during filming of the dating show that made her famous, in a podcast interview released this morning.

Saunders said contestants were filmed up to 16 hours a day and had their phones taken away for the full 10 weeks.

The network has been contacted for comment.

item.title: Inflation figures (DRAFT - embargoed 11.30am)
item.dc:creator: olivia.chen
item.content:encoded:
Headline CPI rose X per cent in the December quarter, the ABS said, taking annual inflation to X per cent.

Trimmed mean inflation, the RBA's preferred measure, was X per cent.

Biggest contributors: electricity, rents, insurance. Fill in from ABS release.

item.title: Storm warning SE Qld
item.dc:creator: hannah.walsh
item.content:encoded:
BOM severe thunderstorm warning for Brisbane, Ipswich, Logan, Gold Coast. Giant hail possible, damaging winds. Expected 3pm to 7pm.

Energex: 12,000 without power in Logan already.

item.title: Have your say: trading hours, story picks and the new timetable
item.content:encoded:
Late-night trading has split the CBD. Traders want longer hours; residents want sleep. Tell us where you stand.

We are planning next month's coverage. Pick up to two.

The new timetable started a fortnight ago. Voting has closed.

item.title: What should we cover next? Readers pick the stories
item.content:encoded: Our newsroom is setting next month's priorities. Pick up to two stories you want us to chase.

item.title: Aussie skiers stranded as record snow buries Japan resort towns
item.dc:creator: sam.obrien
item.content:encoded:
Hundreds of Australian skiers are stranded in Japanese resort towns after a record 2.4m of snow fell in three days.

Roads into Hakuba were closed on Tuesday and JR Hokkaido suspended trains between Sapporo and Kutchan.

Brisbane couple Jess and Mark Tran were due to fly home on Wednesday. "The skiing has been unbelievable. Getting out is another story," Jess said.

Airlines are offering free changes for passengers who cannot reach the airport.
item.excerpt:encoded: Hundreds of Australians in Niseko and Hakuba are stuck after roads and rail lines closed.

item.title: Reality show reunion explodes as cast walks off set
item.dc:creator: mia.fortescue
item.content:encoded:
Filming for the reunion episode of a hit reality dating show was halted after four cast members walked off set, according to sources at the production.

The clash started when one contestant read out private messages sent by another during filming.

It was the most chaotic night of TV I have ever been part of, and I have done six seasons.

Crew member

The network confirmed the episode will air on Sunday night.
item.excerpt:encoded: Two couples refused to film the final scene. Producers say the episode will air 'as it happened'.

item.title: Festival lineup drops with three huge headliners and a first for Aussie music
item.dc:creator: mia.fortescue
item.content:encoded:
Organisers of Byron Bay's biggest winter festival have revealed a lineup that includes three international headliners and, for the first time, an all-Australian closing night.

Tickets go on sale next Thursday at 10am. Three-day passes start at $389.

The festival was cancelled two years ago after floods damaged the site. Organisers said drainage works had been completed.
item.excerpt:encoded: Byron Bay's winter festival returns with an all-Australian closing night.

item.title: Aussie-made horror film tops the US box office
item.dc:creator: mia.fortescue
item.content:encoded:
An Australian horror film shot in Adelaide for less than $4 million has opened at number one in the US, taking $US31 million in its first weekend.

The film, directed by South Australian sisters Kate and Ellie Marsh, beat two big-studio releases.

We shot most of it in our grandmother's house in Unley. She still has not seen it.

Ellie Marsh

It opens in Australian cinemas on Thursday.
item.excerpt:encoded: Shot in Adelaide on a $4m budget, it took $US31m on its opening weekend.

item.title: Inside star's secret $3m Hunter Valley wedding venue
item.dc:creator: mia.fortescue
item.content:encoded:
Matildas veteran Jordan Kemp married her long-time partner at a private vineyard estate in the Hunter Valley on the weekend, with 140 guests asked to hand over their phones at the gate.

The 60-hectare estate near Pokolbin was listed for sale last year at $3.2 million.

Guests included several current Matildas and two former Wallabies captains.

Kemp shared a single black and white photo on Instagram on Monday. It had 400,000 likes by lunchtime.
item.excerpt:encoded: Guests had to hand in their phones at the gate. The vineyard estate costs $40,000 a night to hire.

item.title: 'Slow death': The common food doctors want you to cut
item.dc:creator: grace.liu
item.content:encoded:
Australian doctors are urging people to cut back on processed meats such as ham, bacon and salami, as bowel cancer rates keep climbing among people under 50.

The World Health Organization classifies processed meat as a group 1 carcinogen. Eating 50g a day, about two slices of ham, raises bowel cancer risk by 18 per cent.

Nobody is saying never eat bacon again. But it shouldn't be in your kids' lunchbox every day.

Dr Anna Kowalski, gastroenterologist

Easy swaps

  • Leftover roast chicken instead of deli chicken.
  • Tinned tuna or salmon in sandwiches.
  • Eggs, hummus or cheese for lunchboxes.

Bowel Cancer Australia recommends free screening kits from age 45.
item.excerpt:encoded: Processed meat is a group 1 carcinogen, the same category as tobacco. One ham sandwich a day raises bowel cancer risk by 18 per cent.

item.title: Why your flat white is about to cost $7
item.dc:creator: grace.liu
item.content:encoded:
Australians should expect to pay up to $7 for a flat white by the middle of the year as wholesale coffee prices hit record highs.

Arabica bean prices have more than doubled since early 2024 after droughts in Brazil and Vietnam.

Melbourne cafe owner Gus Romano said he had held his price at $5.20 for 18 months. "Next month it goes to $6. I don't have a choice," he said.

The average price of a small coffee in Australia is $5.10, according to industry data.
item.excerpt:encoded: Coffee bean prices have doubled in two years. Cafe owners say they can't absorb it any longer.

item.title: Aussies are ditching dating apps for run clubs
item.dc:creator: grace.liu
item.content:encoded:
Young Australians are swapping swipes for 5km runs, with social run clubs reporting record numbers as dating app use falls.

Strava data shows run club participation in Australia rose 300 per cent last year.

You chat for 40 minutes, then grab a coffee. It's the least awkward first date there is.

Run club organiser, Sydney

One Bondi club says 11 couples who met on its Saturday runs have since married.
item.excerpt:encoded: Run club sign-ups are up 300 per cent. One Sydney club has had 11 weddings.

item.title: The one screen time rule parents say actually works
item.dc:creator: grace.liu
item.content:encoded:
A Melbourne mum's simple rule for family screen time has been shared more than 200,000 times: every phone goes in a basket from 6pm until breakfast, including the parents'.

Child psychologist Dr Ruth Ambrose said the rule works because it applies to everyone.

Kids notice when the rules are only for them.

Dr Ruth Ambrose
item.excerpt:encoded: Forget timers and apps. A Melbourne family's phone basket has gone viral.

item.title: 'Sleep divorce' trend sweeping Aussie homes
item.dc:creator: grace.liu
item.content:encoded:
One in five Australian couples now sleep in separate beds or rooms, a new survey has found, and most of them say it has improved their relationship.

Snoring was the top reason, followed by different work hours and one partner using a phone in bed.

Sleep researchers say poor sleep raises the risk of arguments the next day.
item.excerpt:encoded: One in five couples now sleep apart. Most say it saved their relationship.

item.title: New Bali rules every Aussie traveller needs to know
item.dc:creator: sam.obrien
item.content:encoded:
Australians heading to Bali are being reminded of new rules that came into force this month, including a tourist levy and on-the-spot fines.

The rules

  • A 150,000 rupiah (about $15) tourist levy, paid online before you fly.
  • Shoulders and knees covered at temples. Sarongs are available at most entrances.
  • Fines for riding a scooter without an international driving permit.
  • No climbing sacred trees or posing for photos on temple shrines.

More than 1.4 million Australians visited Bali last year, more than any other nationality.
item.excerpt:encoded: A new tourist levy, a temple dress code and fines for riding scooters without a licence come into force this month.

item.title: Huge airfare sale: $99 flights across Australia for 72 hours
item.dc:creator: sam.obrien
item.content:encoded:
A major domestic airline has launched a 72-hour sale with one-way fares from $99 on more than 40 routes.

The sale covers travel between February and June. Fares include carry-on bags only.

  • Sydney to Hobart from $99
  • Brisbane to Cairns from $109
  • Melbourne to Gold Coast from $99
  • Perth to Broome from $149

The sale ends at midnight AEDT on Friday.
item.excerpt:encoded: Sydney to Hobart, Brisbane to Cairns and Melbourne to the Gold Coast are all included.

item.title: The Tassie road trip that just topped a global list
item.dc:creator: sam.obrien
item.content:encoded:
A seven-day road trip from Hobart to Cradle Mountain has been named one of the 10 best drives in the world by a major travel guide.

The route takes in Mount Field, Strahan and the Gordon River before finishing at Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park.

You can drive for an hour and not see another car. That's the point.

Tasmanian tour operator
item.excerpt:encoded: Hobart to Cradle Mountain via the west coast has been named one of the world's best drives.

item.title: Massive surprises in Aussie T20 World Cup squad
item.dc:creator: tom.delaney
item.content:encoded:
Selectors have named two uncapped players in Australia's 15-man squad for the T20 World Cup in India and Sri Lanka, and left out a former captain.

Tasmanian fast bowler Riley Grant, 22, has taken 24 wickets in the Big Bash this season at an economy rate of 6.9.

Riley bowls 150km/h and has a yorker that nobody in the BBL can hit. That gets you picked.

Chair of selectors

The squad

The full squad will be confirmed after a fitness test on Monday. The tournament starts on February 7.
item.excerpt:encoded: An uncapped Tasmanian quick is in. A former captain is out.

item.title: AFL star's shock trade request rocks club
item.dc:creator: tom.delaney
item.content:encoded:
A two-time All-Australian midfielder has asked to be traded to a Perth club, despite having four years left on his contract.

The 27-year-old told teammates on Monday that he wanted to move closer to family.

The club said it would not let him go "for anything less than fair value".
item.excerpt:encoded: The two-time All-Australian wants to go home to Western Australia. He has four years left on his contract.

item.title: Aussie teen's fairytale run continues at Melbourne Park
item.dc:creator: tom.delaney
item.content:encoded:
Darwin teenager Ava Brennan has reached the fourth round of the Australian Open as a wildcard, beating the world number 12 in straight sets.

Brennan, 18, had never won a match at a grand slam before this week.

I'm just trying not to look at the draw.

Ava Brennan
item.excerpt:encoded: The 18-year-old wildcard from Darwin is into the fourth round.

item.title: Mid-season sales: the deals actually worth your money this weekend
item.dc:creator: mia.fortescue
item.content:encoded:
Most of the big department stores started their mid-season sales on Thursday night, and several online retailers have matched them.

We tracked prices on 40 popular products over the past three months. About a third of the advertised discounts were smaller than they looked, because the "was" price had gone up a few weeks earlier.

The real bargains

  • Bed linen: down 40 per cent, the lowest price we have seen this year
  • Kitchen appliances: air fryers and stick blenders from $49
  • Activewear: selected lines half price, sizes going fast
  • Kids winter coats: two for $60

Check the price history before you buy. A big red tag does not always mean a big saving.

Consumer advocate, Choice

Most sales run until Sunday night. Some online codes expire at midnight Saturday.
item.excerpt:encoded: Big retailers have cut prices by up to 50 per cent. We checked which discounts are real.

item.title: 'Paid for itself in a month': The $79 air fryer Aussies can't stop buying
item.dc:creator: mia.fortescue
item.content:encoded:
A 5.5 litre air fryer selling for $79 has become one of the best-selling small appliances in the country this year.

Owners say it uses less power than heating a full-size oven for one tray of food. Energy researchers estimate a typical air fryer costs about 10 cents to run for 20 minutes.

Stock was restocked online this morning, with a limit of two per customer.
item.excerpt:encoded: A budget air fryer has sold out three times since January. Owners say it cuts their power bill.

item.title: I tested six linen sheet sets. Only one was worth the price
item.dc:creator: grace.liu
item.content:encoded:
French linen sheets have gone from luxury item to supermarket staple. I slept on six sets over six weeks to find out whether the expensive ones are better.

How I tested

Each set was washed five times on a warm cycle and line dried. I checked for shrinkage, pilling and how soft they felt after each wash.

The $159 set came out on top. It shrank less than 2 centimetres and was the softest after the third wash.

The $420 set was lovely but felt almost identical by the end of the test.
item.excerpt:encoded: Prices ranged from $89 to $420. The winner cost less than half the most expensive set.

item.title: Best running shoes under $150, according to physios
item.dc:creator: grace.liu
item.content:encoded:
Running shoe prices have climbed past $300 for some new models. Physiotherapists say most recreational runners do not need them.

Fit matters more than the price tag. Go to a store late in the day when your feet are at their biggest.

Sports physiotherapist, Melbourne

All of the shoes on this list were under $150 at the time of publishing.
item.excerpt:encoded: You do not need to spend $300 to protect your knees. Three physiotherapists pick their favourites.

item.title: Croc spotted cruising flooded street in north Queensland
item.dc:creator: hannah.walsh
item.content:encoded:
Residents in the north Queensland town of Ingham have been warned to stay out of floodwater after a saltwater crocodile was filmed swimming down a residential street.

Local woman Tash Moretti was filming the water rising outside her home on Thursday morning when the animal appeared. "I thought it was a log until it turned around," she said.

The Herbert River peaked at 14.2m overnight, its highest level since 2019. More than 400 homes have water through them.

Wildlife officers on alert

Queensland wildlife officers said crocodiles often move into new areas during floods and urged residents to report sightings rather than approach the animals.

The Bruce Highway remains cut north and south of the town.
item.excerpt:encoded: Residents in Ingham were filming the rising water when a saltwater crocodile swam past their letterbox.

item.title: Sydney braces for 44C scorcher as heatwave rolls in
item.dc:creator: hannah.walsh
item.content:encoded:
Western Sydney is forecast to hit 44C on Saturday as a severe heatwave moves across NSW, with Penrith tipped to be hotter than Alice Springs.

The Bureau of Meteorology says the hot air mass has been building over central Australia for a week. The city itself is expected to reach 39C before a southerly change late in the afternoon.

Health warning

NSW Health has urged people to check on elderly neighbours, keep pets inside and avoid exercise in the middle of the day.

  • Drink water regularly, even if you do not feel thirsty.
  • Never leave children or pets in parked cars.
  • Close blinds and curtains in the morning.

Energy operators have warned of possible pressure on the grid in the early evening, when air conditioners are running and solar output drops.
item.excerpt:encoded: Western Sydney could be hotter than Alice Springs on Saturday. Here's when the cool change arrives.

item.title: 'Un-Australian': Neighbours at war over nature strip veggie patch
item.dc:creator: hannah.walsh
item.content:encoded:
A Geelong retiree has been told to pull out the vegetable garden he planted on his nature strip after a neighbour complained to the council.

Ron Pappas, 71, built four raised beds on the strip outside his home last spring and grows tomatoes, zucchini and herbs, which he gives away to passers-by.

I've had kids from the primary school picking cherry tomatoes on the way home. How is that a problem?

Ron Pappas

The City of Greater Geelong said nature strip gardens are allowed but must be under 50cm high and leave a clear path for pedestrians. Mr Pappas's beds are 60cm.

A petition supporting him has more than 3000 signatures. The neighbour who complained declined to comment.
item.excerpt:encoded: A Geelong retiree's tomatoes have sparked a council complaint, a petition and 2000 comments on a local Facebook group.

item.title: Perth renters face record 30 applicants for every home
item.dc:creator: olivia.chen
item.content:encoded:
Perth renters are competing with an average of 30 other applicants for every property, new figures show, as the city's vacancy rate falls to 0.4 per cent.

Data from REIWA shows median weekly rents have climbed to $680, up 11 per cent in a year.

Property manager Leanne Ward said she had 64 groups at a single inspection in Scarborough last weekend. "People are offering six months upfront. It's brutal," she said.

What renters can do

  • Have references and payslips ready before the inspection.
  • Apply on the day; most homes are leased within 48 hours.
  • Check the WA rent bidding rules: agents cannot ask you to offer more than the advertised price.

The state government says 3000 social homes will be completed by mid-2027.
item.excerpt:encoded: Vacancy rates in Perth have dropped to 0.4 per cent, and agents say the queue at open homes now runs down the street.

item.title: France to follow Australia's under-16 social media ban
item.dc:creator: ben.matthews
item.content:encoded:
France will introduce a law banning children under 16 from social media, with ministers pointing to Australia's ban as the template.

The French digital minister said platforms would face fines of up to 4 per cent of global turnover if they failed to verify users' ages.

Australia's ban began last December. The eSafety Commissioner says platforms have removed 1.1 million accounts held by under-16s since then.

Australia showed it can be done. Now Europe needs to act together.

French digital minister

Critics in both countries say teenagers are using VPNs and borrowed accounts to get around the rules.
item.excerpt:encoded: French ministers say Australia's law is the model. Tech companies say it doesn't work.

item.title: Why Japan is the cheapest it has been for Aussies in decades
item.dc:creator: sam.obrien
item.content:encoded:
Japan has become one of the best-value destinations for Australians, with the dollar buying more yen than at any time in 35 years.

A bowl of ramen in Tokyo now costs about $9 and a night in a business hotel about $90.

Australian arrivals in Japan hit a record 900,000 last year.
item.excerpt:encoded: The Australian dollar buys more yen than at any time since 1990.

item.title: Cruise passengers confined to cabins after gastro outbreak
item.dc:creator: sam.obrien
item.content:encoded:
More than 200 passengers and crew on a cruise ship returning to Sydney have been told to stay in their cabins after a gastro outbreak.

NSW Health said it would meet the ship when it docks at Circular Quay on Saturday morning.

The cruise line said it had stepped up cleaning and was offering affected passengers a partial refund.
item.excerpt:encoded: More than 200 people on a ship returning to Sydney from New Caledonia have fallen ill.

item.title: The Aussie jobs most exposed to AI, ranked
item.dc:creator: ben.matthews
item.content:encoded:
Clerical and administrative jobs are the most exposed to generative AI, a new government report has found, while trades and care work are the least.

The Jobs and Skills Australia report says AI is more likely to change jobs than replace them outright.

Most exposed

  • Data entry and payroll clerks
  • Call centre workers
  • Paralegals
  • Bookkeepers
  • Copywriters and content producers

Least exposed

  • Electricians and plumbers
  • Aged care and disability workers
  • Nurses
  • Chefs

The question is less "will my job exist" and more "which parts of my job will a machine do".

Report author
item.excerpt:encoded: A new Jobs and Skills Australia report lists the roles most and least likely to change. Some results are surprising.

item.title: New phone price shock for Australian buyers
item.dc:creator: ben.matthews
item.content:encoded:
Australians will pay up to $2899 for the top model of the latest flagship smartphone, $300 more than last year.

The base model starts at $1499. Pre-orders open on Friday.

Telcos are offering trade-in deals worth up to $1000.
item.excerpt:encoded: The top model will cost $2899 here. Is it worth it?

item.title: EV sales surge as petrol tops $2.20 a litre
item.dc:creator: ben.matthews
item.content:encoded:
Electric vehicles made up 12.6 per cent of new car sales last month, a record, as petrol prices topped $2.20 a litre in some capital cities.

Cheaper Chinese-made models are driving the growth. Four EVs now sell for under $40,000.

People come in about the petrol price. Then they do the maths on running costs.

Sydney car dealer
item.excerpt:encoded: One in eight new cars sold last month was electric, a record.

item.title: Scam text warning: fake toll message fooling thousands
item.dc:creator: ben.matthews
item.content:encoded:
Scamwatch has warned of a wave of fake text messages claiming the recipient owes an unpaid road toll.

The messages include a link to a fake payment page that steals card details. Australians lost $2.1 million to the scam last month.

  • Toll companies will never text you a payment link.
  • Check your account by logging in directly, not through the link.
  • Report scam texts by forwarding them to 0429 999 888.
item.excerpt:encoded: Scamwatch has had 18,000 reports in a week. Here is how to spot it.

item.title: Aussie-built rocket set for launch from Arnhem Land
item.dc:creator: ben.matthews
item.content:encoded:
An Australian-built rocket is on the launch pad in Arnhem Land, ready for an attempt to reach orbit as early as Tuesday.

The 23m rocket was designed and built in Queensland. Its first attempt last year ended 14 seconds after lift-off.

The launch window opens at 6am ACST.
item.excerpt:encoded: If it reaches orbit, it will be the first Australian-made rocket to do so from home soil.

item.title: RBA decision: what it means for your mortgage
item.dc:creator: olivia.chen
item.content:encoded:
The Reserve Bank has left the cash rate on hold at 3.60 per cent, saying inflation is moving back toward its target more slowly than expected.

All four major banks had predicted the hold. Most now expect the next cut in May.

What it means for you

For a borrower with a $600,000 loan, monthly repayments stay at about $3,520. A 0.25 point cut would save around $95 a month.

The board needs to see a couple more months of data before it moves again.

Chief economist, major bank

The RBA governor will hold a press conference at 3.30pm AEDT.
item.excerpt:encoded: The cash rate is on hold at 3.60 per cent. Economists now expect the next cut in May.

item.title: Sydney median house price hits $1.7m
item.dc:creator: olivia.chen
item.content:encoded:
Sydney's median house price has reached a record $1.7 million, according to new figures from Cotality.

Brisbane's median house price has overtaken Melbourne's for the first time, at $1.02 million against $985,000.

  • Sydney: $1.70m
  • Brisbane: $1.02m
  • Melbourne: $985,000
  • Perth: $890,000
  • Adelaide: $880,000
item.excerpt:encoded: Prices rose 0.8 per cent in a month. Brisbane overtook Melbourne for the first time.

item.title: The super change hitting millions of Australians in July
item.dc:creator: olivia.chen
item.content:encoded:
From July 1, employers will have to pay superannuation at the same time as wages, rather than quarterly.

The government says the change will add about $6000 to the retirement balance of a typical 25-year-old.

Around $5 billion in super goes unpaid every year, according to the Tax Office.
item.excerpt:encoded: The super guarantee rises and payday super begins. Here is what it means for your balance.

item.title: Fury at China's $1bn beef move
item.dc:creator: olivia.chen
item.content:encoded:
Cattle producers have reacted angrily after China suspended import licences for six Australian meatworks, putting about $1 billion in annual trade at risk.

Chinese customs cited labelling issues. The Agriculture Minister said Australia would seek an urgent explanation.

We found out on a Sunday night from a WeChat message.

Queensland abattoir manager
item.excerpt:encoded: Beijing has suspended licences for six Australian abattoirs. Farmers say they were given no warning.

item.title: Four-day week trial results stun bosses
item.dc:creator: olivia.chen
item.content:encoded:
Twenty-seven of the 30 Australian and New Zealand companies in a six-month four-day week trial have decided to keep it.

Staff sick days fell by a third and revenue held steady, the organisers said.
item.excerpt:encoded: Of 30 Australian companies in the trial, 27 are keeping the shorter week.

item.title: 'Disgrace': A-League match halted as flares rain down
item.dc:creator: daniel.rossi
item.content:encoded:
A-League officials have condemned crowd behaviour after Saturday night's Sydney derby was stopped for 22 minutes when flares were thrown onto the pitch.

One flare landed metres from a goalkeeper. Police entered the players' tunnel at half-time.

This is a disgrace and it will be dealt with.

A-Leagues chief executive

Both clubs face fines and possible point deductions.
item.excerpt:encoded: Play was stopped for 22 minutes and police entered the tunnel after flares were thrown onto the pitch.

item.title: Origin selection bombshell as Blues coach picks rookie fullback
item.dc:creator: daniel.rossi
item.content:encoded:
NSW coach has picked a 20-year-old fullback with 14 NRL games for State of Origin game one, overlooking two current Test players.

The Blues lost last year's series 2-1.
item.excerpt:encoded: A 20-year-old with 14 NRL games is set to start game one.

item.title: Five things to do with your super before June 30
item.dc:creator: olivia.chen
item.content:encoded:
With the end of the financial year approaching, there are a few simple steps that could add thousands to your retirement balance.

  • Use unused concessional caps from the past five years.
  • Check you are not paying for insurance you do not need.
  • Consolidate multiple accounts.
  • Claim a tax deduction for personal contributions.
  • Check your employer has paid what they owe.
item.excerpt:encoded: From catch-up contributions to checking your insurance, here is the end of financial year checklist.

item.title: Moment shark swims metres from swimmers at Gold Coast beach
item.dc:creator: hannah.walsh
item.content:encoded:
Drone footage has captured the moment a large shark swam within metres of a group of swimmers at Burleigh Heads on Sunday morning.

The video, filmed by a local photographer, shows the 2.5m animal gliding parallel to the shore before turning back out to sea. The swimmers did not notice.

Lifeguards closed the beach for an hour as a precaution.

Sharks are always out there. Most of the time they have no interest in us.

Gold Coast lifeguard supervisor

Queensland's shark control program uses drumlines and nets at 86 beaches. The Gold Coast has not had a fatal attack at a netted beach since 1962.
item.excerpt:encoded: Drone footage shows a 2.5m bull shark gliding past a group of unaware swimmers at Burleigh Heads.

item.title: Vets' warning for dog owners as temperatures soar
item.dc:creator: hannah.walsh
item.content:encoded:
Vets are warning dog owners to skip walks in the middle of the day as heatwave conditions spread across southeast Australia.

On a 35C day, footpaths and roads can reach 60C, hot enough to burn paw pads in under a minute.

  • Walk early morning or after sunset.
  • Use the seven-second test: if you can't hold your hand on the ground, it's too hot.
  • Leave out extra water and shade.
  • Watch for heavy panting, drooling and lethargy.
item.excerpt:encoded: Footpaths can reach 60C on a 35C day. Put your hand on the bitumen for seven seconds before a walk.

item.title: Site
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded: This is a fast-paced digital news publisher covering breaking news, politics, business, and culture for a broad, general-interest audience. Its primary readers scan multiple stories at once and often arrive from search or social, so every piece must earn attention in the first few seconds. The newsroom's goals are speed, accuracy, and clarity, and its identity is that of a trusted, independent source of factual, well-sourced reporting.

item.title: Copy
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded: Write in AP style. Lead with the most newsworthy fact (inverted pyramid) — never bury the lede. Use short, punchy sentences and strong active-voice verbs; avoid passive constructions and hedging language like 'may have' or 'reportedly appears to.' Attribute every claim and quote to a named source. Headlines must be clear and scannable, optimized for search and social, but never clickbait — no vague teasers, no all-caps, no excessive punctuation. Keep paragraphs to 1-3 sentences for mobile readability. Avoid jargon; explain acronyms on first use. Do not editorialize or insert opinion into straight news copy.

item.title: Images
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded: Prefer real, on-the-scene photography over stock images or illustrations whenever available, keeping a candid, documentary mood rather than a staged or polished one. Use standard news crop ratios — 16:9 for hero images, 4:3 for inline. Every image needs a cutline (caption) with photographer/source attribution. Avoid images that could be seen as staged or misleading relative to the story.

item.title: Additional
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded: Fact-check every statistic and quote before publishing. Flag anything unverified for editorial review rather than softening it with hedge words. Always attribute quotes to a named, on-record source where possible. Corrections must be appended transparently, not silently edited. Avoid superlatives ('unprecedented', 'historic') unless directly substantiated or quoting a source. Alt text should describe the newsworthy content of an image plainly and factually (who/what/where), not artistic interpretation.

item.title: core/paragraph
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded: Keep paragraphs short — 1 to 3 sentences. One idea per paragraph. Lead each paragraph with the most important information first, in true inverted-pyramid style.

item.title: core/heading
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded: Headlines and subheads must be factual and specific, not clever or vague. Use sentence case. Front-load key terms for SEO and scannability. No clickbait phrasing ('You won't believe...').

item.title: core/image
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded: Include a cutline with source/photographer credit for every image. Alt text describes who/what/where factually. Prefer real photography from the event over stock or illustrated substitutes.

item.title: core/quote
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded: Pull quotes must be verbatim and attributed by full name and title on first reference. Never paraphrase inside a quote block.
